findings.text: root_path is put into a regex without re.escape. If root_path has metacharacters, for example '/a+b' or '/app(1)', the pattern fails to match or raises re.error, so the prefix is not stripped or the request crashes. Use scope['path'].removeprefix(root_path), or check startswith, instead.

The prefix is removed without checking for a path boundary, and without checking that the path starts with root_path at all. With root_path '/app' and path '/application/x', the result is 'lication/x'. That value has no leading slash, so route matching breaks. A root_path of '/' or '' behaves oddly too, because '/' would strip the leading slash from every path.
The new top-level import of starlette.types into _utils risks a circular import if starlette.types ever imports from _utils. Importing it only under TYPE_CHECKING avoids that.

2.reason: This is a hypothetical concern: starlette.types is a leaf module of type aliases that does not import starlette._utils, so the new top-level import creates no circular import (the module is not in ./context/, so this rests on Starlette's known layout).
